sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1! Scroll down directly below this slide to explore our edge versus cloud offloading decision studio.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: In this interactive lab, we can test whether 4G LTE favors local Jetson edge execution, while high-speed 5G flips the latency winner to the cloud!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 2! Scroll down directly below this slide to simulate store-and-forward edge ring buffers during network blackouts.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Here we can model RocksDB NVMe spooling! Watch how a 5,000-packet ring buffer easily absorbs a 60-second outage, but overflows during a 180-second disconnect unless emergency downsampling is enabled.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! An industrial vibration sensor has noise variance of zero point zero four and process variance of ten to the minus four. Calculate the steady-state error variance and Kalman gain.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Time for Checkpoint 1! Remember, solving the algebraic Riccati equation yields the stationary covariance and asymptotic gain.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding deduction! Solving the algebraic Riccati equation yields steady-state error variance of zero point zero zero one nine five and asymptotic Kalman gain of zero point zero four eight eight, slashing noise variance by over 95 percent in constant memory without historical sample arrays!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that steady-state covariance P-infinity is obtained by solving the quadratic Riccati formula, giving zero point zero zero one nine five. The Kalman gain is then computed from P-infinity plus Q divided by the total variance.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! A 300 MFLOP vision workload with a 150 kilobyte payload runs on a 10 GFLOPS edge node versus a 150 GFLOPS cloud cluster. Find the critical crossover bandwidth.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Calculate the allowable upload transmission airtime by subtracting cloud compute from local edge latency.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Brilliant calculation! Local execution requires 30 milliseconds while cloud compute takes only 2 milliseconds. The allowable transmission airtime is 28 milliseconds, setting the crossover bandwidth at 153.6 kilobytes divided by 28 milliseconds, which equals 43.9 megabits per second!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Local edge latency is 30 milliseconds and cloud execution is 2 milliseconds, leaving 28 milliseconds for network transfer. Dividing 153.6 kilobytes by 0.028 seconds yields 43.9 megabits per second.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! An edge gateway receives one-kilobyte packets at 80 Hertz into a 16 megabyte FIFO buffer. Calculate the maximum outage duration before packet loss occurs.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final checkpoint! Convert 16 megabytes into total packet capacity, then divide by the 80 Hertz incoming packet arrival rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Masterclass comprehension! A 16 megabyte buffer stores exactly 16,384 one-kilobyte packets. Arriving at 80 Hertz, the buffer absorbs 16,384 divided by 80, which equals 204.8 seconds—or approximately 3.41 minutes—of complete network outage with zero packet loss!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Sixteen megabytes divided by one kilobyte per packet yields 16,384 packets. Dividing by 80 packets per second yields 204.8 seconds of outage absorption capacity.
